objective_review.claim: Conditional on: The task requires exactly one irreversible external effect; every executed repeated call adds another effect, and no compensating operation is available; Both initial histories are admissible, have identical agent-visible observations, and have no outstanding initial request that can execute later; Recovery can only wait, perform local operations, stop, or repeat the action; it cannot inspect external commitment through another channel; Subsequent calls execute once and return indistinguishable generic acknowledgments in the two histories; Recovery is evaluated within a finite horizon, and policy randomness has the same distribution in both histories. Conditional on the Investigator's five listed assumptions, no observation-limited recovery policy guarantees exactly one external effect in both admissible timeout histories. The optimal worst-case effect-level success probability over those histories is 1/2. Atomic durable deduplication with persistent key reuse changes the contract and ensures exactly one effect if a matching invocation is successfully processed before the evaluation deadline.
objective_review.argument_summary: Cycle 1, Investigator step 34f57df3-e101-426f-a223-28b1123f1944, supplies the complete local argument. Identical observations and coupled randomness imply identical recovery behavior. If R is the additional executed-call count, final counts are R and 1+R; hence success requires disjoint events R=1 and R=0. Their probabilities sum to at most one, and an equal stop/retry mixture attains the bound. The separate deduplication argument derives at-most-once safety from atomic durable recording and at-least-once completion from successful processing. Neither argument establishes implementation behavior or empirical generality.

argument_steps.title: Define the task, tool contract, and success event
argument_steps.argument: The task is to create exactly one irreversible external effect, represented by an integer counter N initially equal to zero. Each executed call to apply(payload) increments N by one; acknowledgments do not reveal N. There is no decrement, cancellation, status query, deduplication, or other observation of N available to the agent. Evaluation occurs at a fixed finite horizon T after recovery terminates. Effect-level success is N=1; truthful completion and safe handling of uncertainty are additional metrics, not substitutes for this condition. Any stronger end-to-end success requirement implies effect-level success, so an upper bound on the latter also bounds the former.

review.rationale: This is a legitimate explicit premise for the conditional claim. Exactly-one effect is a necessary condition for any stronger success criterion, so its probability upper-bounds stronger end-to-end success.

argument_steps.title: Construct the indistinguishable failure pair
argument_steps.argument: In history H0, the initial request is discarded without execution and the client receives a timeout, leaving N=0. In history H1, the initial request executes, its acknowledgment is lost, and the client receives the same timeout, leaving N=1. The local checkpoint, request bytes, timing observations, and all other agent-visible information are identical. The initial request is quiescent in both histories: it cannot execute later. Every subsequent recovery call, if any, executes once and receives the same generic acknowledgment on the same schedule in both histories. These are two admissible schedules under the stated contract, not claims about their prevalence.

review.rationale: Discard-before-execution and commit-with-lost-acknowledgment are both admissible under the stipulated contract. Equal timing, metadata, and subsequent acknowledgments are explicitly imposed, and quiescence excludes a later initial execution that would invalidate the count equations.

argument_steps.title: Adaptive reasoning cannot distinguish these histories
argument_steps.argument: Fix the recovery policy's internal random choices, including stochastic model decisions. Initially its observable state is identical in H0 and H1. If its observed histories remain identical through one step, its next action is identical; a wait, local operation, or repeated call then receives an identical observation by construction. Induction therefore gives identical recovery transcripts and the same number R of additional calls. Removing the conditioning on randomness shows that R has the same distribution in both histories. Checkpoint restoration and a fresh agent run do not invalidate this argument if they have only the specified observations and actions.

review.rationale: Conditioning on the same internal random choices makes the policy's next action a function of identical observable histories. The stipulated response schedule preserves equality inductively. Averaging over the same randomness distribution gives equal distributions of R, including for adaptive policies.

argument_steps.title: Derive the impossibility and tight minimax bound
argument_steps.argument: At the horizon, H0 has N=R and H1 has N=1+R. Success in H0 therefore requires R=1, while success in H1 requires R=0. Consequently s0=Pr(R=1) and s1=Pr(R=0), with s0+s1<=1 and min(s0,s1)<=1/2. The effect-level bound is tight: a policy that makes exactly one additional call with probability 1/2 and otherwise makes none achieves success probability 1/2 in each history. Deterministic stopping yields counts (0,1), one retry yields (1,2), and two or more retries fail in both. If the committed history has a known prior probability p, optimal average effect-level success is max(p,1-p); that prior does not provide a guarantee for each history. Abstention can avoid a false completion claim but cannot guarantee task completion.

review.rationale: The equations N0=R and N1=1+R make the two success events disjoint. Thus min(s0,s1) is at most 1/2, attained by an equal mixture of zero and one retry. With committed-history prior p, average success is p Pr(R=0)+(1-p) Pr(R=1), maximized by selecting the larger coefficient, yielding max(p,1-p). Tightness concerns effect-level success only.

argument_steps.title: Locate the failure propagation and recovery boundary
argument_steps.argument: The initiating fault is loss of information about external commitment, not necessarily an incorrect plan or model judgment. It creates uncertainty between N=0 and N=1. Blind retry converts that uncertainty into a duplicate effect in H1; refusing to retry leaves an omission in H0. Restoring local memory does not restore external state. A more capable model or another critic given the same information cannot eliminate this ambiguity. This does not refute recovery in systems with additional observations, reversible effects, or stronger tool contracts; those systems fall outside the construction.

review.rationale: The count pairs directly demonstrate the propagation boundary: stopping preserves an omission in H0, whereas retrying introduces duplication in H1. Local restoration or additional reasoning cannot distinguish identical information under the same action restrictions.

argument_steps.title: State a sufficient changed contract rather than a universal remedy
argument_steps.argument: Consider instead a tool that accepts a logical-operation key k and immutable payload, atomically couples its effect with a durable record for k, and returns the stored result on every replay. The client durably records k before the first dispatch and reuses it across restarts; the service retains its record throughout the retry horizon. With no other writers, atomic deduplication makes the number of effects for k at most one. If at least one invocation is processed successfully by T, it is also at least one, so N=1. This is a conditional safety-and-completion argument: deduplication alone does not guarantee availability or delivery. Merely attaching a request ID does not establish the contract; an effect followed by a crash before a separate deduplication write still permits duplication.

review.rationale: Under the explicitly changed contract, a durable atomic per-key effect-and-record transition permits at most one effect; successful processing supplies at least one. Persistent key reuse and retention are necessary stated premises. A crash after a separately written effect but before its deduplication record permits replay duplication, as claimed.

argument_steps.title: Specify a discriminating implementation test and independent oracle
argument_steps.argument: Build a controlled append-only effect service with an evaluator-only durable ledger. Inject either discard-before-execution or commit-then-drop-ack, exposing byte-identical timeout transcripts and matched timing to the agent. Test policies that stop, restore-and-retry, restart-and-retry, or replay a persisted key through the atomic service. For deterministic one-retry policies, the predicted baseline effect counts are respectively (0,1), (1,2), and (1,2) across the two faults. Keyed replay predicts (1,1), provided replay processing occurs before the deadline. Also inject a crash between effect creation and a non-atomic deduplication write; duplication would distinguish a genuine atomic contract from a merely labeled idempotency mechanism. The oracle checks actual ledger entries, not the agent's summary. Record false completion, unresolved termination, extra effects, calls, and latency separately. Keep model and prompt versions, task, permissions, deadline, and retry budget fixed; report keyed-service overhead rather than treating it as free. First verify the deterministic service behavior without a model, then use paired seeds to study whether agents actually follow the recovery protocol.

review.rationale: This is a discriminating proposed test, not evidence of execution. Stop and one-retry count pairs follow from the model, while keyed replay predicts one effect in each history only with timely successful processing. The non-atomic crash cut tests a substantive contract difference rather than an interface label.

argument_steps.title: Assess contribution and scope
argument_steps.argument: The contribution is a concrete failure-chain specimen and an exact limit on information-limited recovery, useful for selecting fault-injection cases and rejecting overbroad claims about local checkpointing. It uses a standard indistinguishability argument, not a demonstrated novel recovery architecture. No domain literature, deployed implementation, or agent benchmark has been inspected here, so novelty relative to established work and empirical generality are not assessed. The proposed test evaluates a narrow tool contract; it would not establish overall reliability on long, open-ended tasks.

review.rationale: The contribution is accurately limited to a conditional failure-chain specimen and a test design. No supplied evidence supports novelty, prevalence, or measured benefit, and the step expressly withholds those claims.

artifacts.skeptic_response:
The cycle-2 sensitivity question is answered convincingly under its explicit premises. The count expansion, aggregation, and endpoint constructions are valid. Sharpness is appropriately limited to the supplied rectangular audit information and disagreement budgets; it does not establish an optimal confidence procedure or validate those budgets.

An independent arithmetic check confirms the important finite-cohort distinction. With complete reference auditing and Z=O, the lower difference is (10-floor(90d)-floor(20d))/100 under a common bound d. For every d<0.10, the two floors sum to at most nine. At d=0.10 they sum to eleven, and the stated compatible assignment gives 81 correct A records versus 82 correct B records. Thus the exact threshold is d<0.10, whereas d<1/11 is only the continuous relaxation. This is a constructed sensitivity result, not an observed agent comparison.

The main remaining problem is evidential: no supplied authoritative outcomes justify any practical delta_c. The extension exposes this premise rather than resolving it. The original cycle-1 acceptance-only counterexample remains a valid negative constraint, not a refutation of the audit method. Its supplied extract, e9b2a9ae-e383-4499-8431-4c4ef4b7e5f7, supports that limited conclusion; prior approval is not verification.

A concrete next reduction is to derive the independent oracle-validation sample size required to make this certificate informative. For a cell with n records and d actual Z/Y disagreements, a uniform validation sample of size m observes zero disagreements with probability C(n-d,m)/C(n,m). Inverting this finite-population probability supplies a whole-cell count bound, conditional on validation actually revealing Y. Apply it to the two ranking-threatening cells and determine the smallest validation design that can certify their total disagreement count below ten. This distinguishes a genuinely informative validation plan from repeated reference auditing that cannot constrain shared oracle error.

reasoning_steps.title: Define the target and replace accurate references with bounded disagreement
reasoning_steps.argument: For agent a, fix N_a recorded executions and their binary evaluator decisions O_ai. True correctness Y_ai means that the predeclared external postconditions and constraints hold at horizon H. Z_ai is an imperfect reference label. Both Y and Z are fixed binary attributes of the cohort; auditing reveals Z, not necessarily Y. Partition records into cells c=(a,+) for O=1 and c=(a,-) for O=0, of size n_c. Let T_c=sum Z, S_c=sum Y, and D_c=floor(n_c delta_c), where 0<=delta_c<=1. The substantive oracle premise is sum 1{Z!=Y}<=D_c in every nonempty cell. It imposes neither independent errors nor nondifferential errors. Empty cells contribute zero and require no conditional rate.

reasoning_steps.title: Express simultaneous reference-audit information as feasible counts
reasoning_steps.argument: Suppose the audit supplies intervals [l_c,u_c] such that, with probability at least 1-alpha over audit sampling, every T_c/n_c lies in its interval simultaneously. If m_c records were audited and k_c had Z=1, the observed labels also imply k_c<=T_c<=n_c-m_c+k_c. Consequently define J_c^- = max(k_c,ceil(n_c l_c)) and J_c^+ = min(n_c-m_c+k_c,floor(n_c u_c)). On the simultaneous coverage event, T_c is an integer in [J_c^-,J_c^+]. Exhaustive auditing gives J_c^-=J_c^+=k_c. For an unaudited cell use m_c=k_c=0 and [l_c,u_c]=[0,1]. An empty feasible interval indicates incompatible constraints; it must not be reported as a correctness certificate.

reasoning_steps.title: A reproducible way to obtain the audit coverage premise
reasoning_steps.argument: One conservative construction reuses the finite-population sampling design in the supplied prior extract. For K nonempty cells, prespecify positive sample sizes and sample uniformly without replacement. In a nonexhaustive sampled cell set zhat_c=k_c/m_c, t_c=sqrt(log(2K/alpha)/(2m_c)), and [l_c,u_c]=[max(0,zhat_c-t_c),min(1,zhat_c+t_c)]. The standard without-replacement Hoeffding inequality gives cell failure probability at most 2 exp(-2m_c t_c^2)=alpha/K. Use exact reference prevalence for exhaustive cells and [0,1] for unsampled cells. A union bound establishes simultaneous coverage at least 1-alpha, without independence across cells or agent executions. The result below also accepts other valid simultaneous intervals; it does not claim these conservative intervals are statistically optimal.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive sharp cellwise true-correctness bounds
reasoning_steps.argument: For fixed T_c=t, changing at most D_c binary labels gives max(0,t-D_c)<=S_c<=min(n_c,t+D_c), since each disagreement changes the positive count by at most one. The lower endpoint is attained by changing min(t,D_c) reference-positive labels to zero; the upper endpoint by changing min(n_c-t,D_c) reference-negative labels to one. Optimizing over the feasible reference counts therefore gives B_c^- = max(0,J_c^- - D_c) and B_c^+ = min(n_c,J_c^+ + D_c). These endpoints are attainable: choose a reference vector matching the observed sample and the selected feasible endpoint count, then perform the indicated flips. Every integer between the endpoints is also attainable, because the fixed-t integer intervals overlap or are adjacent as t advances by one. Thus this is an exact projection of the stated cell information, not just a triangle-inequality outer bound.

reasoning_steps.title: Aggregate correctness and differences, with a precise sharpness qualification
reasoning_steps.argument: Set L_a=(sum_{c belonging to a} B_c^-)/N_a and U_a=(sum_{c belonging to a} B_c^+)/N_a. On the simultaneous audit event, p_a=sum_i Y_ai/N_a lies in [L_a,U_a], and p_A-p_B lies in [L_A-U_B,U_A-L_B]. With no additional cross-cell or cross-agent constraints, all lower cell endpoints can be attained together, as can all upper endpoints; choosing A lower and B upper attains the lower difference endpoint, and reversing choices attains the upper. These are therefore sharp interval hulls relative to the supplied rectangular audit bounds, sample observations, and disagreement budgets. A joint audit region or substantive coupling between records could narrow them. A strict A advantage is certified precisely when L_A>U_B; equality permits a tie.

reasoning_steps.title: Separate the simple rate formula from the exact finite-count result
reasoning_steps.argument: Ignoring integer rounding and sample-support tightening, the cell rate bounds are max(0,l_c-delta_c) and min(1,u_c+delta_c). Weighting these by n_c/N_a gives a convenient conservative correctness interval. The exact finite-count formulas above can be narrower. Sharpness here concerns compatible labels given the audit region; it does not mean the audit confidence procedure has minimum width. If delta_c=0, the result reduces to the reference-prevalence certificate. If delta_c=1 in every cell, the result becomes [0,1] for each agent regardless of audit precision.

reasoning_steps.title: Apply the certificate to reference scores of 90 versus 80
reasoning_steps.argument: Use the supplied construction with 100 records per agent, 90 accepted for A and 80 for B, and suppose a complete reference audit gives Z=O. Then A has reference-positive counts (90,0) and B has (80,0) in their accepted/rejected cells. The exact difference interval is [(10-D_A+-D_B-)/100,(10+D_A-+D_B+)/100], where D_A+=floor(90 delta_A+), D_A-=floor(10 delta_A-), D_B+=floor(80 delta_B+), and D_B-=floor(20 delta_B-). Thus A's strict advantage survives exactly when D_A+ + D_B- < 10. Only errors that lower A's accepted-cell correctness or raise B's rejected-cell correctness threaten this certificate; the other two budgets affect its upper endpoint. The rate relaxation certifies A when 0.9 delta_A+ + 0.2 delta_B- < 0.1.

reasoning_steps.title: Check the common-bound threshold and its boundary counterexample exactly
reasoning_steps.argument: If all four cells share the same bound delta=d, the rate relaxation requires d<1/11. The exact 100-record certificate instead holds for every d<0.10: then floor(90d)<=8 and floor(20d)<=1, so the lower difference is at least 1/100. At d=0.10, the allowed counts are 9 and 2, producing lower difference -1/100. This endpoint is attained by flipping nine A accepted references from correct to incorrect and two B rejected references from incorrect to correct, giving true correctness 81% versus 82%. Thus the finite-cohort common-bound threshold is exactly d<0.10, not d<1/11. This difference is an integer-budget effect, not additional evidence about oracle quality. As a check, d=0.05 gives the exact interval [0.05,0.14], from budgets (D_A+,D_A-,D_B+,D_B-)=(4,0,4,1).

reasoning_steps.title: Check the alternative reference audit rather than identifying acceptance with correctness
reasoning_steps.argument: In the second configuration of the supplied example, a full reference audit could instead show 70 reference-positive records in A's accepted cell, zero in A's rejected cell, and B reference counts (80,0). Then U_A=[min(90,70+D_A+)+D_A-]/100 and L_B=(80-D_B+)/100. B's strict advantage is certified exactly when D_B+ + D_A+ + D_A- < 10. To see necessity despite the clipping, if D_A+>=20 then U_A>=0.90>L_B; otherwise the clipping is inactive and the inequality follows directly. Acceptance remains 90 versus 80 in both configurations. The audit distinguishes their Z distributions, but only justified disagreement budgets transfer that distinction into a Y ranking.

reasoning_steps.title: Show what exhaustive auditing cannot identify
reasoning_steps.argument: Without any justified constraint linking Z to Y, hold every observed O, every audited Z, and all nondiagnostic logs fixed. Assign Y=0 to all records or Y=1 to all records; both assignments remain compatible with these observations. More generally every finite-cohort correctness count from 0 through N_a is possible. Across agents, choosing opposite assignments attains differences -1 and +1. Hence the correctness interval hull is [0,1] per agent and the difference interval hull is [-1,1]; neither ranking, false-acceptance rate, nor false-rejection rate is identified. This claim excludes observations that themselves determine Y. More reference audits or agreement among critics with shared blind spots cannot establish a disagreement bound by themselves.

reasoning_steps.title: Keep oracle validation, peer evidence, and deployment inference separate
reasoning_steps.argument: If the delta bounds are themselves simultaneous confidence bounds with failure probability beta, combine that validation event with the reference-audit event to obtain coverage at least 1-alpha-beta by a union bound; no independence is required. This requires actual valid validation evidence for the same target cells, not a guessed delta. The bounded peer extract 29362c57-cbcb-4127-8b3d-3976a3e3e206 discusses hidden external commitment under ambiguous tool timeouts. Its assumptions differ from this measurement model and its source is incomplete, so its probability bound is not transferred. Its warning motivates checking authoritative external state, but does not validate an oracle here. The present result addresses the sensitivity component of o2/o12, while leaving their empirical premise unresolved; o1/o3/o4/o5 and their duplicate ledger entries remain open. reasoning_steps.title: Define the target and replace accurate references with bounded disagreement
reasoning_steps.argument: For agent a, fix N_a recorded executions and their binary evaluator decisions O_ai. True correctness Y_ai means that the predeclared external postconditions and constraints hold at horizon H. Z_ai is an imperfect reference label. Both Y and Z are fixed binary attributes of the cohort; auditing reveals Z, not necessarily Y. Partition records into cells c=(a,+) for O=1 and c=(a,-) for O=0, of size n_c. Let T_c=sum Z, S_c=sum Y, and D_c=floor(n_c delta_c), where 0<=delta_c<=1. The substantive oracle premise is sum 1{Z!=Y}<=D_c in every nonempty cell. It imposes neither independent errors nor nondifferential errors. Empty cells contribute zero and require no conditional rate.

review.rationale: This is an explicit premise of the conditional claim. Because the number of disagreements is integral, a fraction bound delta_c is equivalent to a count bound floor(n_c delta_c). Neither independence nor nondifferential error follows or is needed.

reasoning_steps.title: Express simultaneous reference-audit information as feasible counts
reasoning_steps.argument: Suppose the audit supplies intervals [l_c,u_c] such that, with probability at least 1-alpha over audit sampling, every T_c/n_c lies in its interval simultaneously. If m_c records were audited and k_c had Z=1, the observed labels also imply k_c<=T_c<=n_c-m_c+k_c. Consequently define J_c^- = max(k_c,ceil(n_c l_c)) and J_c^+ = min(n_c-m_c+k_c,floor(n_c u_c)). On the simultaneous coverage event, T_c is an integer in [J_c^-,J_c^+]. Exhaustive auditing gives J_c^-=J_c^+=k_c. For an unaudited cell use m_c=k_c=0 and [l_c,u_c]=[0,1]. An empty feasible interval indicates incompatible constraints; it must not be reported as a correctness certificate.

review.rationale: The audited positives supply a lower support bound k_c, and the remaining unaudited records supply upper bound n_c-m_c+k_c. Intersecting these with the rounded prevalence interval yields exactly the stated feasible integer counts on the coverage event.

reasoning_steps.title: A reproducible way to obtain the audit coverage premise
reasoning_steps.argument: One conservative construction reuses the finite-population sampling design in the supplied prior extract. For K nonempty cells, prespecify positive sample sizes and sample uniformly without replacement. In a nonexhaustive sampled cell set zhat_c=k_c/m_c, t_c=sqrt(log(2K/alpha)/(2m_c)), and [l_c,u_c]=[max(0,zhat_c-t_c),min(1,zhat_c+t_c)]. The standard without-replacement Hoeffding inequality gives cell failure probability at most 2 exp(-2m_c t_c^2)=alpha/K. Use exact reference prevalence for exhaustive cells and [0,1] for unsampled cells. A union bound establishes simultaneous coverage at least 1-alpha, without independence across cells or agent executions. The result below also accepts other valid simultaneous intervals; it does not claim these conservative intervals are statistically optimal.

review.rationale: For fixed positive sample sizes and 0<alpha<1, the without-replacement Hoeffding bound applies to fixed binary cell labels. The chosen radius gives failure probability at most alpha/K per sampled cell; exhaustive and unsampled cells are safely handled, and the union bound needs no cross-cell independence.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive sharp cellwise true-correctness bounds
reasoning_steps.argument: For fixed T_c=t, changing at most D_c binary labels gives max(0,t-D_c)<=S_c<=min(n_c,t+D_c), since each disagreement changes the positive count by at most one. The lower endpoint is attained by changing min(t,D_c) reference-positive labels to zero; the upper endpoint by changing min(n_c-t,D_c) reference-negative labels to one. Optimizing over the feasible reference counts therefore gives B_c^- = max(0,J_c^- - D_c) and B_c^+ = min(n_c,J_c^+ + D_c). These endpoints are attainable: choose a reference vector matching the observed sample and the selected feasible endpoint count, then perform the indicated flips. Every integer between the endpoints is also attainable, because the fixed-t integer intervals overlap or are adjacent as t advances by one. Thus this is an exact projection of the stated cell information, not just a triangle-inequality outer bound.

review.rationale: Each disagreement changes the positive count by at most one. Flipping reference positives or negatives attains the fixed-count endpoints, and every support-feasible reference count can match the observed sample. Adjacent feasible counts generate adjacent or overlapping integer ranges, establishing the claimed projection.

reasoning_steps.title: Aggregate correctness and differences, with a precise sharpness qualification
reasoning_steps.argument: Set L_a=(sum_{c belonging to a} B_c^-)/N_a and U_a=(sum_{c belonging to a} B_c^+)/N_a. On the simultaneous audit event, p_a=sum_i Y_ai/N_a lies in [L_a,U_a], and p_A-p_B lies in [L_A-U_B,U_A-L_B]. With no additional cross-cell or cross-agent constraints, all lower cell endpoints can be attained together, as can all upper endpoints; choosing A lower and B upper attains the lower difference endpoint, and reversing choices attains the upper. These are therefore sharp interval hulls relative to the supplied rectangular audit bounds, sample observations, and disagreement budgets. A joint audit region or substantive coupling between records could narrow them. A strict A advantage is certified precisely when L_A>U_B; equality permits a tie.

review.rationale: Summation and subtraction preserve coverage on the common audit event. With the explicitly stated absence of coupling constraints, cell endpoint assignments can coexist and opposite agent endpoints attain the difference extremes. The qualification to interval hulls avoids claiming every real-valued interior difference is attainable.

reasoning_steps.title: Separate the simple rate formula from the exact finite-count result
reasoning_steps.argument: Ignoring integer rounding and sample-support tightening, the cell rate bounds are max(0,l_c-delta_c) and min(1,u_c+delta_c). Weighting these by n_c/N_a gives a convenient conservative correctness interval. The exact finite-count formulas above can be narrower. Sharpness here concerns compatible labels given the audit region; it does not mean the audit confidence procedure has minimum width. If delta_c=0, the result reduces to the reference-prevalence certificate. If delta_c=1 in every cell, the result becomes [0,1] for each agent regardless of audit precision.

review.rationale: Dropping count rounding and sample-support restrictions can only enlarge the region. Zero disagreement budgets recover the reference bounds, while budgets equal to cell sizes permit every binary correctness vector and hence the full correctness interval.

reasoning_steps.title: Apply the certificate to reference scores of 90 versus 80
reasoning_steps.argument: Use the supplied construction with 100 records per agent, 90 accepted for A and 80 for B, and suppose a complete reference audit gives Z=O. Then A has reference-positive counts (90,0) and B has (80,0) in their accepted/rejected cells. The exact difference interval is [(10-D_A+-D_B-)/100,(10+D_A-+D_B+)/100], where D_A+=floor(90 delta_A+), D_A-=floor(10 delta_A-), D_B+=floor(80 delta_B+), and D_B-=floor(20 delta_B-). Thus A's strict advantage survives exactly when D_A+ + D_B- < 10. Only errors that lower A's accepted-cell correctness or raise B's rejected-cell correctness threaten this certificate; the other two budgets affect its upper endpoint. The rate relaxation certifies A when 0.9 delta_A+ + 0.2 delta_B- < 0.1.

review.rationale: With Z=O, A's lower correctness is (90-D_A+)/100 and B's upper correctness is (80+D_B-)/100. Reversing endpoints gives the stated upper difference. Their subtraction establishes the exact strict-ranking criterion and its conservative rate relaxation.

reasoning_steps.title: Check the common-bound threshold and its boundary counterexample exactly
reasoning_steps.argument: If all four cells share the same bound delta=d, the rate relaxation requires d<1/11. The exact 100-record certificate instead holds for every d<0.10: then floor(90d)<=8 and floor(20d)<=1, so the lower difference is at least 1/100. At d=0.10, the allowed counts are 9 and 2, producing lower difference -1/100. This endpoint is attained by flipping nine A accepted references from correct to incorrect and two B rejected references from incorrect to correct, giving true correctness 81% versus 82%. Thus the finite-cohort common-bound threshold is exactly d<0.10, not d<1/11. This difference is an integer-budget effect, not additional evidence about oracle quality. As a check, d=0.05 gives the exact interval [0.05,0.14], from budgets (D_A+,D_A-,D_B+,D_B-)=(4,0,4,1).

review.rationale: For d<0.10 the threatening integer budgets sum to at most eight plus one; at d=0.10 they are nine plus two. The explicit flips give 81 versus 82 correct records. At d=0.05, budgets (4,0,4,1) yield endpoints 0.05 and 0.14 exactly.

reasoning_steps.title: Check the alternative reference audit rather than identifying acceptance with correctness
reasoning_steps.argument: In the second configuration of the supplied example, a full reference audit could instead show 70 reference-positive records in A's accepted cell, zero in A's rejected cell, and B reference counts (80,0). Then U_A=[min(90,70+D_A+)+D_A-]/100 and L_B=(80-D_B+)/100. B's strict advantage is certified exactly when D_B+ + D_A+ + D_A- < 10. To see necessity despite the clipping, if D_A+>=20 then U_A>=0.90>L_B; otherwise the clipping is inactive and the inequality follows directly. Acceptance remains 90 versus 80 in both configurations. The audit distinguishes their Z distributions, but only justified disagreement budgets transfer that distinction into a Y ranking.

review.rationale: B's lower endpoint is (80-D_B+)/100 and A's upper endpoint is the supplied clipped expression. When D_A+<20, direct subtraction gives the stated condition; when D_A+>=20, A's upper endpoint is already at least 0.90, preventing certification of B's superiority.

reasoning_steps.title: Show what exhaustive auditing cannot identify
reasoning_steps.argument: Without any justified constraint linking Z to Y, hold every observed O, every audited Z, and all nondiagnostic logs fixed. Assign Y=0 to all records or Y=1 to all records; both assignments remain compatible with these observations. More generally every finite-cohort correctness count from 0 through N_a is possible. Across agents, choosing opposite assignments attains differences -1 and +1. Hence the correctness interval hull is [0,1] per agent and the difference interval hull is [-1,1]; neither ranking, false-acceptance rate, nor false-rejection rate is identified. This claim excludes observations that themselves determine Y. More reference audits or agreement among critics with shared blind spots cannot establish a disagreement bound by themselves.

Opposite assignments across agents attain difference endpoints -1 and 1. The exclusion of observations that determine Y is essential and explicitly stated.

objective_review.argument_summary: Cycle 1, artifact e9b2a9ae-e383-4499-8431-4c4ef4b7e5f7, steps 2–3 supplies the measurement identity and acceptance-only ranking counterexample; its steps 5–6 supplies the sampling design reused here. Cycle 2 steps 2–5 intersects audit intervals with feasible integer reference counts, expands those counts by the permitted label flips, and attains all relevant endpoints independently across cells. Steps 7–9 correctly specialize the bounds to both synthetic reference configurations, including the integer-budget threshold. Step 10 establishes nonidentification without an oracle-error restriction. Step 11 separates statistical coverage from oracle validation and deployment inference. These complete the requested conditional analytical extension, not the broader empirical research objective.

argument_steps.title: Define the target and replace accurate references with bounded disagreement
argument_steps.argument: For agent a, fix N_a recorded executions and their binary evaluator decisions O_ai. True correctness Y_ai means that the predeclared external postconditions and constraints hold at horizon H. Z_ai is an imperfect reference label. Both Y and Z are fixed binary attributes of the cohort; auditing reveals Z, not necessarily Y. Partition records into cells c=(a,+) for O=1 and c=(a,-) for O=0, of size n_c. Let T_c=sum Z, S_c=sum Y, and D_c=floor(n_c delta_c), where 0<=delta_c<=1. The substantive oracle premise is sum 1{Z!=Y}<=D_c in every nonempty cell. It imposes neither independent errors nor nondifferential errors. Empty cells contribute zero and require no conditional rate.

review.rationale: This is an explicit premise of the conditional claim. Because the number of disagreements is integral, a fraction bound delta_c is equivalent to a count bound floor(n_c delta_c). Neither independence nor nondifferential error follows or is needed.

argument_steps.title: Express simultaneous reference-audit information as feasible counts
argument_steps.argument: Suppose the audit supplies intervals [l_c,u_c] such that, with probability at least 1-alpha over audit sampling, every T_c/n_c lies in its interval simultaneously. If m_c records were audited and k_c had Z=1, the observed labels also imply k_c<=T_c<=n_c-m_c+k_c. Consequently define J_c^- = max(k_c,ceil(n_c l_c)) and J_c^+ = min(n_c-m_c+k_c,floor(n_c u_c)). On the simultaneous coverage event, T_c is an integer in [J_c^-,J_c^+]. Exhaustive auditing gives J_c^-=J_c^+=k_c. For an unaudited cell use m_c=k_c=0 and [l_c,u_c]=[0,1]. An empty feasible interval indicates incompatible constraints; it must not be reported as a correctness certificate.

review.rationale: The audited positives supply a lower support bound k_c, and the remaining unaudited records supply upper bound n_c-m_c+k_c. Intersecting these with the rounded prevalence interval yields exactly the stated feasible integer counts on the coverage event.

argument_steps.title: A reproducible way to obtain the audit coverage premise
argument_steps.argument: One conservative construction reuses the finite-population sampling design in the supplied prior extract. For K nonempty cells, prespecify positive sample sizes and sample uniformly without replacement. In a nonexhaustive sampled cell set zhat_c=k_c/m_c, t_c=sqrt(log(2K/alpha)/(2m_c)), and [l_c,u_c]=[max(0,zhat_c-t_c),min(1,zhat_c+t_c)]. The standard without-replacement Hoeffding inequality gives cell failure probability at most 2 exp(-2m_c t_c^2)=alpha/K. Use exact reference prevalence for exhaustive cells and [0,1] for unsampled cells. A union bound establishes simultaneous coverage at least 1-alpha, without independence across cells or agent executions. The result below also accepts other valid simultaneous intervals; it does not claim these conservative intervals are statistically optimal.

review.rationale: For fixed positive sample sizes and 0<alpha<1, the without-replacement Hoeffding bound applies to fixed binary cell labels. The chosen radius gives failure probability at most alpha/K per sampled cell; exhaustive and unsampled cells are safely handled, and the union bound needs no cross-cell independence.

argument_steps.title: Derive sharp cellwise true-correctness bounds
argument_steps.argument: For fixed T_c=t, changing at most D_c binary labels gives max(0,t-D_c)<=S_c<=min(n_c,t+D_c), since each disagreement changes the positive count by at most one. The lower endpoint is attained by changing min(t,D_c) reference-positive labels to zero; the upper endpoint by changing min(n_c-t,D_c) reference-negative labels to one. Optimizing over the feasible reference counts therefore gives B_c^- = max(0,J_c^- - D_c) and B_c^+ = min(n_c,J_c^+ + D_c). These endpoints are attainable: choose a reference vector matching the observed sample and the selected feasible endpoint count, then perform the indicated flips. Every integer between the endpoints is also attainable, because the fixed-t integer intervals overlap or are adjacent as t advances by one. Thus this is an exact projection of the stated cell information, not just a triangle-inequality outer bound.

review.rationale: Each disagreement changes the positive count by at most one. Flipping reference positives or negatives attains the fixed-count endpoints, and every support-feasible reference count can match the observed sample. Adjacent feasible counts generate adjacent or overlapping integer ranges, establishing the claimed projection.

argument_steps.title: Aggregate correctness and differences, with a precise sharpness qualification
argument_steps.argument: Set L_a=(sum_{c belonging to a} B_c^-)/N_a and U_a=(sum_{c belonging to a} B_c^+)/N_a. On the simultaneous audit event, p_a=sum_i Y_ai/N_a lies in [L_a,U_a], and p_A-p_B lies in [L_A-U_B,U_A-L_B]. With no additional cross-cell or cross-agent constraints, all lower cell endpoints can be attained together, as can all upper endpoints; choosing A lower and B upper attains the lower difference endpoint, and reversing choices attains the upper. These are therefore sharp interval hulls relative to the supplied rectangular audit bounds, sample observations, and disagreement budgets. A joint audit region or substantive coupling between records could narrow them. A strict A advantage is certified precisely when L_A>U_B; equality permits a tie.

review.rationale: Summation and subtraction preserve coverage on the common audit event. With the explicitly stated absence of coupling constraints, cell endpoint assignments can coexist and opposite agent endpoints attain the difference extremes. The qualification to interval hulls avoids claiming every real-valued interior difference is attainable.

argument_steps.title: Separate the simple rate formula from the exact finite-count result
argument_steps.argument: Ignoring integer rounding and sample-support tightening, the cell rate bounds are max(0,l_c-delta_c) and min(1,u_c+delta_c). Weighting these by n_c/N_a gives a convenient conservative correctness interval. The exact finite-count formulas above can be narrower. Sharpness here concerns compatible labels given the audit region; it does not mean the audit confidence procedure has minimum width. If delta_c=0, the result reduces to the reference-prevalence certificate. If delta_c=1 in every cell, the result becomes [0,1] for each agent regardless of audit precision.

review.rationale: Dropping count rounding and sample-support restrictions can only enlarge the region. Zero disagreement budgets recover the reference bounds, while budgets equal to cell sizes permit every binary correctness vector and hence the full correctness interval.

argument_steps.title: Apply the certificate to reference scores of 90 versus 80
argument_steps.argument: Use the supplied construction with 100 records per agent, 90 accepted for A and 80 for B, and suppose a complete reference audit gives Z=O. Then A has reference-positive counts (90,0) and B has (80,0) in their accepted/rejected cells. The exact difference interval is [(10-D_A+-D_B-)/100,(10+D_A-+D_B+)/100], where D_A+=floor(90 delta_A+), D_A-=floor(10 delta_A-), D_B+=floor(80 delta_B+), and D_B-=floor(20 delta_B-). Thus A's strict advantage survives exactly when D_A+ + D_B- < 10. Only errors that lower A's accepted-cell correctness or raise B's rejected-cell correctness threaten this certificate; the other two budgets affect its upper endpoint. The rate relaxation certifies A when 0.9 delta_A+ + 0.2 delta_B- < 0.1.

review.rationale: With Z=O, A's lower correctness is (90-D_A+)/100 and B's upper correctness is (80+D_B-)/100. Reversing endpoints gives the stated upper difference. Their subtraction establishes the exact strict-ranking criterion and its conservative rate relaxation.

argument_steps.title: Check the common-bound threshold and its boundary counterexample exactly
argument_steps.argument: If all four cells share the same bound delta=d, the rate relaxation requires d<1/11. The exact 100-record certificate instead holds for every d<0.10: then floor(90d)<=8 and floor(20d)<=1, so the lower difference is at least 1/100. At d=0.10, the allowed counts are 9 and 2, producing lower difference -1/100. This endpoint is attained by flipping nine A accepted references from correct to incorrect and two B rejected references from incorrect to correct, giving true correctness 81% versus 82%. Thus the finite-cohort common-bound threshold is exactly d<0.10, not d<1/11. This difference is an integer-budget effect, not additional evidence about oracle quality. As a check, d=0.05 gives the exact interval [0.05,0.14], from budgets (D_A+,D_A-,D_B+,D_B-)=(4,0,4,1).

review.rationale: For d<0.10 the threatening integer budgets sum to at most eight plus one; at d=0.10 they are nine plus two. The explicit flips give 81 versus 82 correct records. At d=0.05, budgets (4,0,4,1) yield endpoints 0.05 and 0.14 exactly.

argument_steps.title: Check the alternative reference audit rather than identifying acceptance with correctness
argument_steps.argument: In the second configuration of the supplied example, a full reference audit could instead show 70 reference-positive records in A's accepted cell, zero in A's rejected cell, and B reference counts (80,0). Then U_A=[min(90,70+D_A+)+D_A-]/100 and L_B=(80-D_B+)/100. B's strict advantage is certified exactly when D_B+ + D_A+ + D_A- < 10. To see necessity despite the clipping, if D_A+>=20 then U_A>=0.90>L_B; otherwise the clipping is inactive and the inequality follows directly. Acceptance remains 90 versus 80 in both configurations. The audit distinguishes their Z distributions, but only justified disagreement budgets transfer that distinction into a Y ranking.

review.rationale: B's lower endpoint is (80-D_B+)/100 and A's upper endpoint is the supplied clipped expression. When D_A+<20, direct subtraction gives the stated condition; when D_A+>=20, A's upper endpoint is already at least 0.90, preventing certification of B's superiority.

argument_steps.title: Show what exhaustive auditing cannot identify
argument_steps.argument: Without any justified constraint linking Z to Y, hold every observed O, every audited Z, and all nondiagnostic logs fixed. Assign Y=0 to all records or Y=1 to all records; both assignments remain compatible with these observations. More generally every finite-cohort correctness count from 0 through N_a is possible. Across agents, choosing opposite assignments attains differences -1 and +1. Hence the correctness interval hull is [0,1] per agent and the difference interval hull is [-1,1]; neither ranking, false-acceptance rate, nor false-rejection rate is identified. This claim excludes observations that themselves determine Y. More reference audits or agreement among critics with shared blind spots cannot establish a disagreement bound by themselves.

review.rationale: If observed information imposes no restriction on Y, the all-zero and all-one assignments preserve every O and Z observation. Opposite assignments across agents attain difference endpoints -1 and 1. The exclusion of observations that determine Y is essential and explicitly stated.

argument_steps.title: Keep oracle validation, peer evidence, and deployment inference separate
argument_steps.argument: If the delta bounds are themselves simultaneous confidence bounds with failure probability beta, combine that validation event with the reference-audit event to obtain coverage at least 1-alpha-beta by a union bound; no independence is required. This requires actual valid validation evidence for the same target cells, not a guessed delta. The bounded peer extract 29362c57-cbcb-4127-8b3d-3976a3e3e206 discusses hidden external commitment under ambiguous tool timeouts. Its assumptions differ from this measurement model and its source is incomplete, so its probability bound is not transferred. Its warning motivates checking authoritative external state, but does not validate an oracle here. The present result addresses the sensitivity component of o2/o12, while leaving their empirical premise unresolved; o1/o3/o4/o5 and their duplicate ledger entries remain open. Novelty, practical benefit, and deployment generality have not been assessed.

review.rationale: Intersecting audit and valid simultaneous validation events gives failure probability at most alpha+beta without independence. The step does not transfer the peer's truncated probability claim and correctly leaves empirical validation, deployment inference, and broader reliability obligations open.

artifacts.strategy_title: Understand failure propagation and recovery in autonomous AI agents
artifacts.claim_or_question: No: under the stated asynchronous, non-idempotent execution model, a linearizable commitment-status query does not suffice for guaranteed exactly-one recovery. NOT_FOUND means that the initial request has not committed at the query's linearization point, not that it cannot commit later. A discarded request and a pending request can therefore require incompatible recovery actions. A sufficient stronger contract is durable cancellation serialized with the actual external effect: it must either certify the existing commitment or permanently prevent that request from committing. This provides at-most-one safety; exactly-one completion additionally requires successful processing and, for confirmed completion, delivery of the relevant responses.
artifacts.method: Analytical schedule construction and state-machine invariant proof; no experiment is executed or requested. The hypothesis is that observing absence of commitment is weaker than establishing final nonexecution. The competing claim predicts that retry after a linearizable NOT_FOUND is safe; an explicit schedule in which the old request commits after the replacement discriminates against it. Retain the prior model's irreversible effect, absence of compensation, single recovery controller, and exactly-once execution of subsequent acknowledged calls; relax initial-request quiescence and add the proposed commitment query. Then specify a stronger cancellation contract and prove safety separately from conditional completion. The supplied bounded extract of artifact 29362c57-cbcb-4127-8b3d-3976a3e3e206 was inspected, not its saved original or an implementation. Its earlier probability bound is not transferred to this changed observation model.
assumptions: For the negative result: effects are irreversible and additive; there is no compensation, deduplication across distinct requests, or other effect-producing writer.
The initial request may be permanently discarded or delayed for an arbitrarily long time after timeout and NOT_FOUND; each dispatched request executes at most once.

The read-only status query is linearizable with actual commitment, has durable accurate commitment records, and neither exposes pending work nor prevents later commitment. Recovery has no additional channel certifying final nonexecution.

Recovery uses a single controller. Subsequent replacement invocations retain the base model's exactly-once processing and acknowledgment guarantee; unknown outcomes do not themselves constitute confirmed completion.

For the sufficient changed-contract result: seal and actual effect commitment obey the atomic durable OPEN/COMMITTED/CANCELLED specification, including absent-request tombstones, immutable identity and payload, exclusion of delayed workers, and retention throughout the possible execution lifetime.

For conditional completion: seal eventually returns a terminal result, and any authorized replacement is successfully processed and acknowledged. Completion by a finite deadline additionally requires these events by that deadline.
artifacts.evidence_status: Analytical counterexample and conditional state-machine proof; no execution, external-source retrieval, or formal verification occurred. The supplied prior and peer extracts are not independently verified implementation evidence.
artifacts.skeptic_response:
The cycle-2 analytical result is convincing but unverified. A linearizable read establishes noncommitment at one instant, not permanent nonexecution. The legal order status(r) < commit(r') < commit(r) gives two effects after an accurate NOT_FOUND reply. The discarded execution requires a replacement for completion, while an arbitrarily delayed original can duplicate that replacement. Finite waiting and repeated read-only queries do not remove this conflict.

The proposed seal contract resolves the race under explicitly stronger premises. Serialization of seal with the actual effect leaves only two terminal branches: COMMITTED prohibits replacement; CANCELLED permanently prohibits the original and permits at most one replacement. This establishes at-most-one safety independently of message delivery. Exactly-one and confirmed completion additionally require the stated progress and response-delivery assumptions. No finite deadline follows from linearizability alone.

An independent boundary check also supports the warning about superficial fencing: a worker can pass a token check, pause, receive cancellation at the wrapper, then commit downstream after a replacement. Thus the invariant requires exclusion at the actual effect boundary, not merely a cancellation endpoint or upstream token check.

The local question is answered, but the project remains partial. No implementation, controlled recovery comparison, literature inspection, or empirical agent-reliability result is supplied. The principal next uncertainty is whether a wrapper around a nonparticipating irreversible downstream tool can provide the proposed cancellation guarantee while also resolving recovery. The next cycle should isolate that boundary analytically rather than repeat the completed status-query argument.

reasoning_steps.title: Define the execution and observation contract
reasoning_steps.argument: Let N initially be zero. Executing the initial request r or a replacement r' creates one irreversible effect and increments N. Each individual dispatched request executes at most once, but different requests are not deduplicated against one another. There are no other effect-producing writers or compensations. A client timeout need not terminate r. Give the proposed status interface its strongest relevant read semantics: status(r) is linearizable with r's actual effect commitment, returns COMMITTED with a durable result if that commitment precedes its linearization point, and otherwise returns NOT_FOUND. It does not report pending execution or inhibit future commitment. The commitment record has no visibility gap or expiration during the analysis. Thus the counterexample does not depend on stale reads or non-atomic recording.

reasoning_steps.title: Construct the discarded schedule
reasoning_steps.argument: Choose ordered events t0<t1<t2<t3<t4<t5<T. At t0 the client dispatches r. In schedule D, r is permanently discarded without execution. At t1 the client observes a timeout. At t2 status(r) linearizes and at t3 returns NOT_FOUND. At t4 recovery dispatches r'; at t5 r' executes and is acknowledged. N(T)=1. No observation of the initial timeout or NOT_FOUND proves that this discarded schedule, rather than a delayed schedule, occurred.

reasoning_steps.title: Construct the pending schedule with the same recovery prefix
reasoning_steps.argument: In schedule P, r is retained but not executed through t5. The timeout, query invocation, NOT_FOUND reply, replacement execution, acknowledgment, timing, and metadata through t5 match D. The query is legal: r had not committed at t2. At a further event t6 with t5<t6<T, r executes, and its acknowledgment is lost. Hence N(T)=2. An independent check is the legal linearization order status(r) < commit(r') < commit(r): the read and both effects satisfy their specifications. There is no contradiction with linearizability.

reasoning_steps.title: Establish the safety-versus-completion obstruction beyond one retry policy
reasoning_steps.argument: Consider any finite recovery prefix ending in its first replacement dispatch on a discarded execution. Before that dispatch, a pending execution can have exactly the same observations: postpone r's commitment past every completed status query and every wait in the prefix. The replacement can then commit, followed by r, producing two effects. Thus any policy that permits such a replacement prefix cannot guarantee at-most-one safety for all admissible schedules. Conversely, never replacing r cannot achieve exactly-one completion in D. Repeated queries and finite waiting merely lengthen the indistinguishable prefix. A randomized policy cannot give a zero-error guarantee by assigning positive probability to an unsafe replacement decision; this argument asserts no numerical minimax bound for the changed model. Waiting indefinitely avoids this particular duplicate but abandons completion in D.

reasoning_steps.title: Identify the precise propagation mechanism and scope change
reasoning_steps.argument: The failure chain is timeout → accurate observation of current noncommitment → unjustified inference of final nonexecution → replacement → delayed original commitment → duplicate effect. This is a check-then-act race, not a stale-query fault or necessarily a reasoning-capability deficit. A post-retry query may detect the duplicate but cannot undo an irreversible effect. The prior artifact excluded pending initial requests and status queries, so its count equations and 1/2 bound are not premises here. Its narrow conclusion about local state not restoring external state remains compatible with this new construction. A status operation that also closes execution is outside the read-only contract and is precisely the stronger mechanism considered next.

reasoning_steps.title: Specify a sufficient durable cancellation contract
reasoning_steps.argument: Associate r and its immutable payload with durable state S_r in {OPEN, COMMITTED(result), CANCELLED}, initially logically OPEN even if the request has not arrived. All effect attempts and seal(r) operations serialize on this state. commit(r) may create its effect only by an atomic transition OPEN → COMMITTED(result) that includes the actual irreversible effect. If S_r is CANCELLED or COMMITTED, it creates no further effect. seal(r) atomically changes OPEN → CANCELLED and returns CANCELLED, or returns the existing COMMITTED result or CANCELLED state without changing it. A cancellation tombstone must be created even when r is absent from the server, survive crashes, and remain effective for every possible delayed arrival or worker. Repeating seal after a lost reply is safe. Neither terminal state expires while an old request can still execute.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive the recovery protocol and its race outcomes
reasoning_steps.argument: After the timeout, invoke seal(r); do not dispatch a replacement until its terminal outcome is known. If it returns COMMITTED, accept that result and issue no replacement. If it returns CANCELLED, dispatch at most one replacement r', using the base model's guarantee that this subsequent invocation executes once and returns its acknowledgment. There are only two possible race orders from OPEN. If commit(r) wins, N becomes one and every seal returns COMMITTED. If seal(r) wins, r is permanently unable to increment N and a replacement is permitted. A timeout of seal is not a CANCELLED result: recovery repeats seal or remains unresolved rather than speculating.

reasoning_steps.title: Prove at-most-one safety independently of progress
reasoning_steps.argument: Before recovery, r contributes at most one effect. After a COMMITTED seal outcome, the protocol issues no replacement and r's terminal state prevents further effects. After a CANCELLED seal outcome, r contributes zero effects for the entire execution: it could not have committed before that outcome, since COMMITTED is terminal, and cannot commit afterward. The controller then issues at most one replacement, which contributes at most one effect. These cases imply N≤1 at every time, including after recovery terminates and after any evaluation deadline. Communication loss may block progress but cannot violate this invariant if an unknown seal outcome never authorizes a replacement. This proves safety for arbitrary ordering of r and seal under the specified contract.

reasoning_steps.title: Prove conditional completion and distinguish knowledge from effects

argument_steps.title: Define the execution and observation contract
argument_steps.argument: Let N initially be zero. Executing the initial request r or a replacement r' creates one irreversible effect and increments N. Each individual dispatched request executes at most once, but different requests are not deduplicated against one another. There are no other effect-producing writers or compensations. A client timeout need not terminate r. Give the proposed status interface its strongest relevant read semantics: status(r) is linearizable with r's actual effect commitment, returns COMMITTED with a durable result if that commitment precedes its linearization point, and otherwise returns NOT_FOUND. It does not report pending execution or inhibit future commitment. The commitment record has no visibility gap or expiration during the analysis. Thus the counterexample does not depend on stale reads or non-atomic recording.

review.rationale: Accepted as an explicit premise of the conditional claim, not as an established tool guarantee. Accurate linearizable commitment reads can return NOT_FOUND before a pending effect without exposing or cancelling that work.

argument_steps.title: Construct the discarded schedule
argument_steps.argument: Choose ordered events t0<t1<t2<t3<t4<t5<T. At t0 the client dispatches r. In schedule D, r is permanently discarded without execution. At t1 the client observes a timeout. At t2 status(r) linearizes and at t3 returns NOT_FOUND. At t4 recovery dispatches r'; at t5 r' executes and is acknowledged. N(T)=1. No observation of the initial timeout or NOT_FOUND proves that this discarded schedule, rather than a delayed schedule, occurred.

review.rationale: Permanent discard leaves zero original effects, and the stipulated successful replacement adds one. The timeout and read response do not certify that the original was discarded.

argument_steps.title: Construct the pending schedule with the same recovery prefix
argument_steps.argument: In schedule P, r is retained but not executed through t5. The timeout, query invocation, NOT_FOUND reply, replacement execution, acknowledgment, timing, and metadata through t5 match D. The query is legal: r had not committed at t2. At a further event t6 with t5<t6<T, r executes, and its acknowledgment is lost. Hence N(T)=2. An independent check is the legal linearization order status(r) < commit(r') < commit(r): the read and both effects satisfy their specifications. There is no contradiction with linearizability.

review.rationale: Delaying the original until after replacement acknowledgment preserves the stated observable prefix. The order status(r), commit(r'), commit(r) respects the read specification and gives N=2 before T.

argument_steps.title: Establish the safety-versus-completion obstruction beyond one retry policy
argument_steps.argument: Consider any finite recovery prefix ending in its first replacement dispatch on a discarded execution. Before that dispatch, a pending execution can have exactly the same observations: postpone r's commitment past every completed status query and every wait in the prefix. The replacement can then commit, followed by r, producing two effects. Thus any policy that permits such a replacement prefix cannot guarantee at-most-one safety for all admissible schedules. Conversely, never replacing r cannot achieve exactly-one completion in D. Repeated queries and finite waiting merely lengthen the indistinguishable prefix. A randomized policy cannot give a zero-error guarantee by assigning positive probability to an unsafe replacement decision; this argument asserts no numerical minimax bound for the changed model. Waiting indefinitely avoids this particular duplicate but abandons completion in D.

review.rationale: For any finite prefix reaching replacement in the discarded history, arbitrary original-request delay reproduces all preceding observations. Scheduling both effects afterward violates safety; never replacing fails completion on permanent discard. The step properly avoids transferring a numerical minimax bound.

argument_steps.title: Identify the precise propagation mechanism and scope change
argument_steps.argument: The failure chain is timeout → accurate observation of current noncommitment → unjustified inference of final nonexecution → replacement → delayed original commitment → duplicate effect. This is a check-then-act race, not a stale-query fault or necessarily a reasoning-capability deficit. A post-retry query may detect the duplicate but cannot undo an irreversible effect. The prior artifact excluded pending initial requests and status queries, so its count equations and 1/2 bound are not premises here. Its narrow conclusion about local state not restoring external state remains compatible with this new construction. A status operation that also closes execution is outside the read-only contract and is precisely the stronger mechanism considered next.

review.rationale: The schedules locate the invalid inference precisely: current absence is treated as final nonexecution. The supplied cycle-1 extract explicitly required initial-request quiescence and excluded status queries, so its count equations are not applicable to this changed model.

argument_steps.title: Specify a sufficient durable cancellation contract
argument_steps.argument: Associate r and its immutable payload with durable state S_r in {OPEN, COMMITTED(result), CANCELLED}, initially logically OPEN even if the request has not arrived. All effect attempts and seal(r) operations serialize on this state. commit(r) may create its effect only by an atomic transition OPEN → COMMITTED(result) that includes the actual irreversible effect. If S_r is CANCELLED or COMMITTED, it creates no further effect. seal(r) atomically changes OPEN → CANCELLED and returns CANCELLED, or returns the existing COMMITTED result or CANCELLED state without changing it. A cancellation tombstone must be created even when r is absent from the server, survive crashes, and remain effective for every possible delayed arrival or worker. Repeating seal after a lost reply is safe. Neither terminal state expires while an old request can still execute.

review.rationale: Accepted only as the explicitly conditional stronger-contract premise. Terminal durable states, absent-request tombstones, and atomic coupling to the actual effect exclude both late arrival after cancellation and replay after commitment. No implementation compliance follows.

argument_steps.title: Derive the recovery protocol and its race outcomes
argument_steps.argument: After the timeout, invoke seal(r); do not dispatch a replacement until its terminal outcome is known. If it returns COMMITTED, accept that result and issue no replacement. If it returns CANCELLED, dispatch at most one replacement r', using the base model's guarantee that this subsequent invocation executes once and returns its acknowledgment. There are only two possible race orders from OPEN. If commit(r) wins, N becomes one and every seal returns COMMITTED. If seal(r) wins, r is permanently unable to increment N and a replacement is permitted. A timeout of seal is not a CANCELLED result: recovery repeats seal or remains unresolved rather than speculating.

review.rationale: Serialization admits exactly the two stated winning transitions from OPEN. The protocol authorizes replacement only after a known CANCELLED outcome; repeating seal after an unknown response cannot create an effect under the specification.

argument_steps.title: Prove at-most-one safety independently of progress
argument_steps.argument: Before recovery, r contributes at most one effect. After a COMMITTED seal outcome, the protocol issues no replacement and r's terminal state prevents further effects. After a CANCELLED seal outcome, r contributes zero effects for the entire execution: it could not have committed before that outcome, since COMMITTED is terminal, and cannot commit afterward. The controller then issues at most one replacement, which contributes at most one effect. These cases imply N≤1 at every time, including after recovery terminates and after any evaluation deadline. Communication loss may block progress but cannot violate this invariant if an unknown seal outcome never authorizes a replacement. This proves safety for arbitrary ordering of r and seal under the specified contract.

review.rationale: COMMITTED permits one original effect and no replacement. CANCELLED implies no past or future original effect and permits at most one replacement effect. These exhaustive cases prove N≤1 independently of progress, including after the observation deadline.

argument_steps.title: Prove conditional completion and distinguish knowledge from effects
argument_steps.argument: Suppose repeated seal invocations eventually receive a terminal response. A COMMITTED response already certifies N=1. A CANCELLED response leaves N=0, and successful processing of the single replacement makes N=1; its acknowledgment permits confirmed completion. Thus eventual confirmed completion requires both eventual resolution of seal and, on the cancelled branch, successful replacement processing and response delivery. No finite deadline follows merely from linearizability or cancellation. For completion by T, those branch-specific events must occur by T; known latency bounds could establish this, whereas fairness alone cannot. If a replacement acknowledgment can also be lost, the base model's reliable-subsequent-call premise no longer holds: unresolved recovery recurs for r', and this single-replacement protocol does not establish confirmed completion in that enlarged domain.

review.rationale: A delivered COMMITTED result certifies one effect; delivered cancellation followed by successful replacement processing gives one effect, and acknowledgment supplies confirmation. Eventual delivery does not imply any fixed deadline, and losing replacement acknowledgments leaves the enlarged problem unresolved as stated.

argument_steps.title: Exclude superficially similar but insufficient cancellation and fencing mechanisms
argument_steps.argument: Cancellation that only removes queued work is insufficient if an already-running worker can still commit. Likewise, checking a fencing token before a network call is insufficient: a worker can pass the check, pause, be fenced out, and later complete the irreversible effect downstream. The required exclusion must hold at the actual effect boundary, or a cancellation barrier must wait for all earlier authorized work to settle and report COMMITTED if any committed. A cancellation ACK meaning only 'request received' does not certify CANCELLED. These distinctions explain why the state machine is a sufficient specification, not evidence that an ordinary cancellation endpoint implements it.

review.rationale: A worker that passes an upstream check before cancellation can still perform a later downstream effect. Therefore queue removal, token prechecks, and receipt acknowledgments do not entail permanent nonexecution. A sufficient barrier must settle or exclude previously authorized work at the effect boundary.

argument_steps.title: Specify the next discriminating check and assess the contribution

assumptions: For the impossibility result, original and replacement effects are irreversible and additive; each dispatched request executes at most once, distinct requests are not deduplicated, and there are no other writers or compensations.

No available channel certifies permanent original-request nonexecution. Any available read-only commitment query may accurately report absence while the original remains pending.

The wrapper continues executing with reliable durable local operations. Guarantees range over all admissible downstream schedules; the argument uses deterministic policies or fixes policy randomness when requiring pointwise guarantees.

CANCELLED authorizes replacement only if the original has produced no effect and cannot produce any later. Conclusive resolution means a truthful COMMITTED or sound CANCELLED result, not UNKNOWN, escalation, or mere process termination.

For the separate sufficient participation result only, seal and actual commitment satisfy the durable effect-boundary serialization and terminal exclusion contract. This is not assumed of the original downstream tool.

For the separate sufficient quiescence result only, a trustworthy barrier excludes every future original effect, new wrapper dispatches remain closed, and a complete accurate post-barrier observation establishes whether an original effect occurred.

For liveness under either changed contract, the requisite terminal evidence eventually arrives. Confirmed task completion additionally requires successful processing and acknowledgment of any authorized single replacement.
artifacts.evidence_status: Analytical conditional impossibility and sufficiency arguments; no implementation, runtime execution, external-source retrieval, or formal verification occurred. Prior and peer extracts remain unverified and incomplete; the target original was not supplied.
artifacts.skeptic_response:
The cycle-3 local result is convincing but unverified. In the discarded execution, conclusive resolution must eventually return CANCELLED because no actual commitment exists. At that finite decision prefix, a downstream execution delayed until afterward has the same wrapper records, fencing epochs, clocks, and absence replies. It therefore receives the same authorization, although the original can still commit. The legal order CANCELLED < replacement effect < original effect produces two irreversible effects. Durable local state does not exclude this continuation.

This establishes a contract-level safety–liveness obstruction, not universal recovery impossibility. Waiting or returning UNKNOWN can preserve safety but does not meet the explicitly defined conclusive-resolution requirement. The randomized scope is appropriately restricted to pointwise guarantees; no almost-sure or numerical bound is established.

The proposed escape conditions are sound as conditional specifications. Effect-boundary serialization can exclude late execution. Alternatively, certified quiescence plus a complete post-barrier outcome observation can establish both past outcome and future exclusion. Neither component alone suffices: quiescence can follow an unrecorded commitment, while an accurate zero read can precede a late effect. Eventual evidence delivery is an additional liveness premise, and replacement acknowledgment is needed for confirmed task completion.

The peer handoff is useful only as a narrowed methodological complement. Fixed-horizon correctness auditing and permanent execution exclusion have different domains. The paired histories also demonstrate why wrapper-label agreement alone cannot validate an oracle-disagreement budget. No peer interval, probability theorem, or omitted derivation is transferred.
