strategy_findings.strategy_title: Develop a rigorous framework for measuring AI agent reliability
strategy_findings.claim: Conditional on: The cohorts and binary O, Z, Y labels are fixed, equally weighted, correctly linked to records, and defined under a frozen external-correctness rubric and observation horizon H; Validation actually reveals Y for every selected record through complete, accurate actual-effect evidence and correct rubric application by H; it does not merely reveal another fallible reference label; The proposed bounded validation environment supplies a justified terminal boundary and complete relevant event history; its availability is an unvalidated premise, not an observed property of an existing tool; Validation sample sizes, allocation, and error allowances are prespecified, with uniform sampling without replacement from each targeted whole cell and no outcome-dependent stopping or exclusions; For the 43-label numerical result, complete reference inspection establishes Z=O across the cohort, so reference-audit failure allowance is zero, and validation observes no disagreements; The minimum is restricted to separate hypergeometric zero-disagreement upper bounds combined through a union bound, with freely prespecified error allocation; it is not an optimum over all joint statistical procedures. Conditional on authoritative validation labels, fixed finite cohorts, prespecified uniform sampling without replacement, and cohort-wide knowledge that Z=O, zero observed disagreements in 23 uniformly selected A-accepted records and a census of B's 20 rejected records support a 95% simultaneous certificate that p_A-p_B is at least 0.01. The minimum of 43 holds within the declared separate-cell hypergeometric-bound and union-bound procedure after repairing the omitted b=2,t=15 case. This is a planned design, not an observed reliability result or a global sample-complexity optimum.

reasoning_steps.title: Define the population, labels, and ranking-threatening cells
reasoning_steps.argument: There are 100 fixed records per agent. A has 90 accepted and 10 rejected records; B has 80 accepted and 20 rejected records. O is evaluator acceptance, Z is the fixed reference label, and Y is binary external correctness under the frozen rubric and horizon H. Let d_c be the actual whole-cell number of Z/Y disagreements. When Z=O throughout the cohort, A has at least 90-d_A+ correct records and B has at most 80+d_B- correct records. Therefore p_A-p_B >= (10-d_A+-d_B-)/100. Errors in A's rejected cell or B's accepted cell cannot worsen this lower bound. They need not be validated for this one-sided claim.

review.rationale: With Z=O, at most d_A+ of A's 90 accepted records are incorrect, and at most d_B- of B's 20 rejected records add correctness beyond its 80 accepted records. Other cells can only improve this one-sided lower difference.

reasoning_steps.title: Specify an independently grounded validation stage
reasoning_steps.argument: Before drawing samples, freeze record identities, cell membership, Z labels, model/prompt/tool versions, budgets, rubric, and H. Prespecify sample sizes and randomization; sample uniformly without replacement from every targeted whole cell, not merely from previously convenient audit records. Validation obtains Y from external state and constraint-relevant event history, not from completion text or a second model's agreement. A concrete admissible domain is a closed transactional sandbox whose actual-effect ledger and immutable terminal snapshot completely determine the rubric. Its declared execution window must leave enough time for bounded drain or effect fencing, terminal inspection, and adjudication by H. The validator is operationally separate from the agent and reference evaluator, and blinded to agent identity where feasible. Sampling or validation must not alter the original outcome. These are proposed requirements, not demonstrated capabilities of a supplied system.

review.rationale: This is an explicit premise of the conditional claim, not evidence of an existing implementation. Sampling the frozen whole cells avoids convenience-sample selection, and preserving original outcomes is necessary for the stated finite-population target.

reasoning_steps.title: State precisely what makes a validation label authoritative
reasoning_steps.argument: Authority requires a justified correspondence between the observed records and every rubric-relevant actual effect: correct record identity and timestamps, complete observation of all relevant writers and side effects, accurate durable history, correct postcondition checks, and enough history to detect intermediate constraint violations as well as terminal failure. A terminal snapshot alone is insufficient when earlier forbidden effects matter. All selected records must be ascertainable; unavailable evidence cannot be silently excluded or labeled as agreement. A replay ordinarily labels a new execution, not the original one. In the proposed bounded sandbox, terminated or fenced writers make the inspected terminal state stable through H. An unbounded asynchronous service without such a contract does not satisfy this premise merely because a status query says NOT_FOUND. Outcomes beyond the declared rubric/horizon remain outside the claim.

review.rationale: The authority premise explicitly requires complete rubric-relevant actual-effect history and correct identity linkage. It correctly distinguishes original-execution ascertainment from replay and terminal-state correctness from earlier safety violations. None of these capabilities is established empirically.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive the zero-disagreement sampling probability
reasoning_steps.argument: In a fixed cell of size n containing d disagreements, a size-m uniform sample has X disagreements. Exactly C(n-d,m) of the C(n,m) possible samples contain none. Thus h(n,m,d)=P_d(X=0)=C(n-d,m)/C(n,m)=C(n-m,d)/C(n,d), taking a binomial coefficient as zero when its lower argument exceeds its upper argument. This is a whole-population statement under random sampling; it requires no independent errors or independent agent executions. For fixed n,m, h is nonincreasing in d. The two expressions independently count the same event by selecting agreement records or placing all disagreements outside the sample.

review.rationale: Counting samples entirely within the n-d agreement records gives C(n-d,m)/C(n,m). Counting disagreement placements outside the sample gives the equivalent expression. Both depend on uniform sampling, not independence of record errors.

reasoning_steps.title: Invert the probability into a valid count bound
reasoning_steps.argument: Prespecify a cell error allowance beta with 0<beta<1. On observing X=0, define U(n,m;beta)=max{d in {0,...,n}: h(n,m,d)>beta}; on X>0, return the conservative bound n. For a fixed true d, undercoverage can occur only when X=0 and d>U. Monotonicity then gives P_d(undercoverage)=h(n,m,d)<=beta. Consequently d<=U has unconditional coverage at least 1-beta. This confidence statement is not a posterior probability conditional on observing zero. At m=0 the bound is n. A census reveals d exactly; for a zero-disagreement census use U=0 with failure allowance zero. For nonzero observations, a prespecified full hypergeometric inversion could replace the deliberately conservative fallback.

review.rationale: For fixed d above the reported zero-event upper bound, monotonicity implies h(n,m,d)<=beta. Undercoverage then occurs only on the zero-event branch, with probability at most beta. The fallback n cannot undercover, and a census can reveal d exactly.

reasoning_steps.title: Obtain simultaneous coverage and compose with reference auditing
reasoning_steps.argument: For prespecified validation allowances beta_c, the union bound gives P(all d_c<=U_c)>=1-sum_c beta_c. No independence between cells, validation labels, or agent runs is required. Let the reference audit simultaneously cover every cell's reference-positive count T_c by [J_c^-,J_c^+] with failure probability at most alpha. On the intersection event, each true-positive count lies between max(0,J_c^- - U_c) and min(n_c,J_c^+ + U_c). Aggregating those endpoints gives correctness and difference bounds with coverage at least 1-alpha-sum_c beta_c. Overlap or dependence between reference auditing and validation is allowed provided each procedure retains its claimed marginal coverage. Outcome-driven changes to sample sizes or error allocations are not justified by this fixed-design argument.

review.rationale: A union bound combines valid marginal coverage events without independence. On their intersection, each disagreement changes the positive count by at most one, yielding the stated expanded count endpoints. Untargeted cells can retain trivial bounds.

reasoning_steps.title: Make the optimization criterion explicit
reasoning_steps.argument: For the numerical design, complete reference inspection establishes Z=O, hence alpha=0. A positive lower difference requires U_A+ + U_B- <=9. Write their proposed upper limits as a and b with a+b=9; using smaller sums cannot improve feasibility. To achieve these limits after zero observations, it suffices and, for these inverted bounds, is necessary that h(90,m_A,a+1)<=beta_A and h(20,m_B,b+1)<=beta_B. With freely prespecified nonnegative allowances totaling at most 1/20, the feasibility criterion is therefore h(90,m_A,10-b)+h(20,m_B,b+1)<=1/20 for some integer b=0,...,9. Zero allowance here is used for an exact census. This specifies the procedure class in which the minimum is claimed.

review.rationale: Strict superiority requires integer upper counts summing to at most nine. For proposed limits a and b, inversion requires the first excluded counts a+1 and b+1 to have zero-event probabilities within the allocated allowances. Their sum is therefore the correct feasibility test for this rectangular, union-bound procedure.

reasoning_steps.title: Construct the 43-label certificate
reasoning_steps.argument: Prespecify m_A=23, m_B=20, beta_A=1/20 and beta_B=0. B's zero-disagreement census establishes d_B-=0 exactly. For A, h(90,23,10)=C(67,10)/C(90,10)<1/20, while h(90,23,9)=C(67,9)/C(90,9)>1/20. Thus the inverted upper bound is U_A+=9. On the 95% coverage event, p_A>=81/100 and p_B<=80/100, so p_A-p_B>=1/100. This certifies a strict finite-cohort advantage, not equivalence to a 90% versus 80% true-correctness comparison.

review.rationale: The two binomial-ratio inequalities place A's inverted bound at nine; B's census gives zero. Substitution gives A at least 81 correct records and B at most 80 on the 95% coverage event. This does not assert that the true rates equal their acceptance rates.

reasoning_steps.title: Exclude totals of 42 or fewer: boundary and low-b cases
reasoning_steps.argument: Because h decreases with sample size, it suffices to exclude total 42; any smaller design can be augmented to 42. Put t=m_B and m_A=42-t. For b=0, B's probability is (20-t)/20, forcing t>=19. At t=19 it already consumes 1/20 and A's probability is positive; at t=20, A's probability is C(68,10)/C(90,10)>1/20. For b=1, requiring each probability individually to be at most 1/20 forces 16<=t<=17: B excludes t<=15, while A excludes t>=18 since C(66,9)/C(90,9)>1/20. Throughout this remaining range their sum is at least C(64,9)/C(90,9)+3/190>1/20. For b=2 the analogous necessary range is 12<=t<=14. Throughout it the sum is at least C(60,8)/C(90,8)+20/1140>1/20. These are exact rational comparisons, obtained by cross multiplication.

review.rationale: The b=0 and b=1 exclusions are valid, and the stated b=2 lower bound excludes t=12,13,14. However, the claimed b=2 necessary range omits t=15.
review.objection: C(63,8)/C(90,8)<1/20, so t=15 passes A's individual probability constraint. It must be excluded using the combined probability. That sum exceeds 1/20, as shown in this review, so the conclusion is recoverable without changing the proposed design.

reasoning_steps.title: Complete the minimum proof
reasoning_steps.argument: For b=3, individual probability constraints force 10<=t<=11. Throughout that range the sum is at least C(58,7)/C(90,7)+126/4845>1/20. For b=4, the individual constraints require m_A>=35 and m_B>=9, already totaling at least 44: C(56,6)/C(90,6)>1/20 and C(12,5)/C(20,5)>1/20 establish the necessary thresholds. For b=5 they require m_A>=40 and m_B>=7, totaling at least 47: use C(51,5)/C(90,5)>1/20 and C(14,6)/C(20,6)>1/20. For b>=6, A's tested count 10-b is at most four, and even m_A=42 gives h>=C(48,4)/C(90,4)>1/20. All b are excluded at total 42. Together with the construction, this proves the minimum 43 within the declared procedure class.

review.rationale: The stated thresholds exclude b=3 through b=9: the remaining b=3 range fails the sum constraint, b=4 and b=5 already require totals above 42, and b>=6 fails A's individual constraint even with 42 A samples. Together with the explicitly repaired b=2 case, these exclusions establish the restricted minimum.

reasoning_steps.title: Explain error-budget and method sensitivity
reasoning_steps.argument: The minimum uses asymmetric allocation: an exact census of the small threatening cell and all statistical error allowance in the larger cell. It must not be reported as a result for a fixed equal-tail design. If both cells are assigned beta=0.025 in advance, a feasible design is m_A=32,m_B=14, with upper counts eight and one respectively; that is a different design. If reference auditing spends alpha>0, validation has only 0.05-alpha available, and feasibility must be recomputed using that smaller budget. The 43-label construction remains valid only when alpha+C(67,10)/C(90,10)<=0.05. A nonrectangular joint confidence region or an additional independence assumption could change the optimum; no global sample-complexity optimality is asserted.

review.rationale: Asymmetric error allocation and the need to include reference-audit failure probability are correctly identified. The equal-tail example remains feasible, but its individual inverted counts are incorrect.
review.objection: At beta=0.025, m_A=32 gives U_A=7 and m_B=14 gives U_B=2, not eight and one. Also, allocating alpha addresses coverage only; sampled reference information must still be propagated through its actual count region.

reasoning_steps.title: Evaluate the evidence-linked peer handoff without transferring its theorem
reasoning_steps.argument: I examined the supplied bounded source extract 496ed077-19aa-4a3d-a216-0a51cf23c866 and target extract e9b2a9ae-e383-4499-8431-4c4ef4b7e5f7. The target's explicit worlds preserve acceptance while changing correctness from 90 versus 80 to 70 versus 80, so its acceptance/correctness distinction is directly applicable here. The source instead concerns pending irreversible requests, linearizable status, and a proposed stronger cancellation contract. A request can be uncommitted at a query or finite inspection and still commit later; this independently explains why a current-status record cannot certify eventual nonexecution. I adopt the handoff's limited observational warning, not its truncated cancellation proof or any implementation guarantee. It changes the validation specification by requiring actual-effect history and a justified terminal boundary, but not the hypergeometric inference or its sample minimum. The domains overlap in oracle design, not in execution guarantees. The source's incomplete extract remains unverified.

review.rationale: The supplied peer assumptions allow a pending request to commit after an accurate absence query. This supports the limited warning about terminal boundaries, while the finite-cohort target establishes only an acceptance/correctness distinction. The step appropriately transfers neither the truncated recovery proof nor implementation guarantees.

reasoning_steps.title: Locate the contribution and preserve unresolved obligations
reasoning_steps.argument: This advances the design component of oracle-validation obligations o2/o12/o49/o55, but does not close their empirical premise or the execution obligations o3/o51/o56. The ledger's benchmark-inspection, deployment, severity, recovery, tool-quality, and resource obligations remain unresolved. The addressed acceptance-only negative result is preserved; it is not a refutation of authoritative validation. The supplied cycle-2 skeptic response and peer artifacts are incomplete extracts, so no omitted argument is assumed resolved. This is a standard exact finite-population inference technique specialized to an agent-evaluation certificate, with a procedure-specific minimum derivation. Literature novelty, practical benefit, and empirical generality are not assessed.

review.rationale: The current work advances conditional validation design while expressly leaving oracle implementation, executed auditing, deployment inference, and broader reliability dimensions open. The supplied prior derivations support this limited continuity; prior agreement is not treated as verification.

strategy_findings.skeptic_response:
The hypergeometric inversion and dependence-free coverage argument are sound under the stated authority and fixed-sampling premises. The 23-plus-20 construction gives the claimed conditional 95% certificate. No validation was executed, and no supplied external-state evidence establishes that practical validation labels reveal Y.

Two arithmetic errors require correction. In step 9, the b=2 necessary range includes t=15, not just 12 through 14: C(63,8)=3,872,894,697 and C(90,8)=77,515,521,435, so 20 C(63,8)=77,457,893,940<C(90,8). Thus A's individual zero-disagreement probability at m_A=27 is slightly below 0.05. This does not invalidate the claimed minimum: the missing case has combined probability C(63,8)/C(90,8)+C(5,3)/C(20,3)>1/20. For example, the first term exceeds 9/200 and the second exceeds 1/200. The supplied lower bound still excludes t=12,13,14. This repairs the omitted boundary case and preserves the procedure-specific minimum of 43.

In step 11, the equal-tail example m_A=32,m_B=14 yields inverted bounds seven and two, not eight and one. For A, C(58,8)/C(90,8)<1/40 while C(58,7)/C(90,7)>1/40. For B, C(6,2)/C(20,2)=3/38>1/40 while C(6,3)/C(20,3)=1/57<1/40. Their sum is still nine, so the example remains feasible after correction. These are analytical arithmetic checks, not runtime executions.

The strongest remaining uncertainty is the authority premise, not statistical independence. A complete reference census and additional fallible critics cannot establish complete observation of actual effects. The peer handoff usefully narrows the validation requirements to actual-effect history and a justified terminal boundary; its truncated recovery theorem supplies neither an implemented oracle nor a cancellation guarantee here. The next useful reduction is an explicit task-level validation contract that can distinguish transient violations hidden by an identical terminal snapshot.

strategy_findings.strategy_title: Understand failure propagation and recovery in autonomous AI agents
strategy_findings.claim: Conditional on: For the impossibility result, original and replacement effects are irreversible and additive; each dispatched request executes at most once, distinct requests are not deduplicated, and there are no other writers or compensations; An already-dispatched original request may be permanently discarded or delayed for an arbitrarily long finite time. Downstream execution does not check wrapper fencing tokens or serialize its effect with wrapper record updates; No available channel certifies permanent original-request nonexecution. Any available read-only commitment query may accurately report absence while the original remains pending; The wrapper continues executing with reliable durable local operations. Guarantees range over all admissible downstream schedules; the argument uses deterministic policies or fixes policy randomness when requiring pointwise guarantees; CANCELLED authorizes replacement only if the original has produced no effect and cannot produce any later. Conclusive resolution means a truthful COMMITTED or sound CANCELLED result, not UNKNOWN, escalation, or mere process termination; For the separate sufficient participation result only, seal and actual commitment satisfy the durable effect-boundary serialization and terminal exclusion contract. This is not assumed of the original downstream tool; For the separate sufficient quiescence result only, a trustworthy barrier excludes every future original effect, new wrapper dispatches remain closed, and a complete accurate post-barrier observation establishes whether an original effect occurred; For liveness under either changed contract, the requisite terminal evidence eventually arrives. Confirmed task completion additionally requires successful processing and acknowledgment of any authorized single replacement. Conditional on the Investigator's listed execution, observation, authorization, and pointwise-guarantee assumptions, wrapper-only durability and fencing cannot guarantee both sound CANCELLED authorization and eventual conclusive original-request resolution. Effect-boundary participation, or certified quiescence combined with complete authoritative outcome observation, supplies sufficient changed contracts when the listed progress premises also hold. This resolves the local analytical question, not the project's empirical reliability objective.

reasoning_steps.title: Define the effect, authorization, and progress contracts
reasoning_steps.argument: Let E_r(t) be the number of actual irreversible effects of the original request r by time t, initially zero and restricted to {0,1}. A distinct replacement r' can independently add one effect, with no cross-request deduplication or compensation. Sound CANCELLED at time t means that r has produced no effect and cannot produce one in any admissible continuation after authorization. COMMITTED must certify an actual effect, not merely a wrapper record or dispatch. Conclusive-resolution liveness requires an eventual known COMMITTED or sound CANCELLED outcome on every admissible execution. Exactly-one task completion further requires that any authorized replacement execute and, for confirmed completion, that its outcome become known.

review.rationale: Accepted as definitions and explicit premises of the conditional claim. Permanent nonexecution is stronger than present noncommitment, and conclusive original-request resolution is correctly distinguished from task completion and acknowledgment.

reasoning_steps.title: Isolate the uncontrolled downstream boundary
reasoning_steps.argument: The wrapper can durably record r, prevent new wrapper dispatches, increment fencing epochs, and reject stale local workers. But r has already crossed that boundary: downstream may discard it permanently or retain it for an arbitrarily long finite delay before executing. The downstream effect neither consults the wrapper's current token nor serializes with its record updates. No available observation certifies permanent downstream nonexecution. If read-only commitment queries exist, grant them accurate linearizable answers: an uncommitted pending request and a discarded request both yield absence. These premises are stronger for the wrapper than unreliable local storage, but still permit the required paired histories.

review.rationale: Accepted as the stipulated model, not a demonstrated service property. Once a request crosses the wrapper boundary, local fencing cannot constrain a downstream effect that does not consult it. Accurate absence reads remain compatible with both discard and pending execution.

reasoning_steps.title: Construct the discarded execution
reasoning_steps.argument: In execution D, the wrapper durably records r with token e, dispatches it, and receives a timeout after downstream discards r without effect. The wrapper continues running and all its local operations finish. Every commitment query reports absence. Thus E_r remains zero forever. A truthful COMMITTED result is impossible in D. If conclusive-resolution liveness holds, the wrapper must eventually return CANCELLED at some finite event τ. Its entire visible prefix through τ includes records, token values, query replies, clocks, timing, and any locally generated cancellation acknowledgment.

review.rationale: Permanent discard makes truthful COMMITTED unavailable. Under the stated two-outcome conclusive-resolution requirement, eventual resolution therefore entails CANCELLED at a finite event, providing the prefix needed for the construction.

reasoning_steps.title: Construct an indistinguishable delayed execution
reasoning_steps.argument: In execution P, downstream retains the dispatched r but performs no effect through τ. Schedule the same wrapper steps, clock observations, query replies, and local responses as in D. Inductively, identical visible input and identical policy choices yield identical wrapper state and outputs: record writes and fencing increments therefore also match. The absence queries are legal because r has not committed. The wrapper consequently returns the same CANCELLED authorization at τ. After τ, downstream executes r without consulting the now-revoked token. This is an allowed continuation of P and contradicts the authorization's permanent-nonexecution meaning.

review.rationale: An arbitrarily long finite downstream delay can extend past the chosen finite event. Identical observations and fixed policy choices reproduce local state and output; absence reads remain legal before commitment. The subsequent original effect directly violates CANCELLED's specified meaning.

reasoning_steps.title: Check the user-visible consequence independently
reasoning_steps.argument: Suppose the authorized replacement executes once and is acknowledged between τ and the delayed original's execution. In D the final total E_r + E_r' is 0 + 1 = 1. In P it is 1 + 1 = 2. The event order dispatch(r) < timeout < local revoke < CANCELLED < effect(r') < effect(r) is consistent with every stated interface: none constrains the final downstream effect by the local revoke. This explicit legal ordering independently checks the indistinguishability argument. Even without replacement, the late effect already falsifies CANCELLED; replacement converts that false certificate into a duplicate irreversible action.

review.rationale: The stated ordering obeys the nonparticipating downstream contract. One replacement effect gives totals one in the discarded execution and two in the delayed execution. The authorization is already false without replacement, so the proof does not depend on replacement liveness.

reasoning_steps.title: Separate safety, liveness, and administrative termination
reasoning_steps.argument: Therefore no universally sound wrapper can return CANCELLED at any finite prefix of D: each such prefix has a delayed continuation like P. It also cannot truthfully return COMMITTED in D. Waiting preserves safety but violates conclusive-resolution liveness there. Returning UNKNOWN, escalating, or stopping can be safe administrative termination, but is not authorization for replacement and does not satisfy the defined resolution guarantee. A finite evaluation deadline does not eliminate the hazard: r can execute after that deadline. The argument covers deterministic policies and guarantees required for every fixed random tape; no numerical probability bound or almost-sure termination theorem is claimed.

review.rationale: Every finite discarded prefix permits the delayed continuation, excluding universally sound cancellation there. COMMITTED is also unavailable, so waiting or UNKNOWN cannot satisfy the defined resolution requirement. The step explicitly avoids extending the fixed-random-tape argument to an almost-sure theorem.

reasoning_steps.title: Identify the logically necessary information
reasoning_steps.argument: Let Compatible(h) be the executions consistent with a visible history h at authorization. A necessary condition for sound CANCELLED is that every execution in Compatible(h), under every allowed continuation, has zero original effects. Hence a useful cancellation certificate must establish both no prior effect and exclusion of every future original effect. Local revocation establishes only that no new compliant wrapper dispatch is allowed; it does not satisfy either external-state claim for the outstanding call. To restore conclusive resolution in discarded executions, some such distinguishing certificate must also eventually become obtainable. This is a semantic requirement, not a claim that there is one uniquely weakest API.

review.rationale: Sound authorization requires zero original effects in every execution and continuation compatible with the observed history. This separates the necessary past-outcome and future-exclusion facts without asserting a uniquely minimal API.

reasoning_steps.title: Give a sufficient downstream-participation contract
reasoning_steps.argument: One sufficient changed contract is the cycle-2 seal specification: the actual effect and durable per-request state transition serialize, with terminal COMMITTED and CANCELLED states. Seal must return COMMITTED if the effect won, or durably prevent every later effect attempt if cancellation won, including delayed arrivals and already-authorized work. If COMMITTED wins, issue no replacement and the total is one. If CANCELLED wins, the original contributes zero forever, so at most one single-execution replacement preserves total ≤ 1. Eventual delivery of a terminal seal result gives conclusive original-request resolution; replacement processing and acknowledgment are additional premises for confirmed task completion. A token check followed by an independently scheduled effect is insufficient because cancellation can occur between them. This is a sufficient specification only, not an implementation established for the stipulated downstream tool.

review.rationale: The supplied cycle-2 seal specification serializes terminal state with the actual effect. COMMITTED permits no replacement; CANCELLED excludes the original and permits at most one single-execution replacement. These cases establish safety, while terminal response delivery and replacement acknowledgment are separate progress premises.

reasoning_steps.title: Give an alternative certified-quiescence contract
reasoning_steps.argument: Atomic effect-record coupling is not logically necessary if a different authoritative mechanism closes the uncertainty. Suppose a certificate at barrier b proves that no old downstream attempt can produce an effect after b, and the wrapper has durably closed all new dispatch paths for r. Then obtain an accurate, complete observation of r's actual effect count after b. If the count is zero, CANCELLED is sound: there was no past effect and the barrier excludes future ones. If it is one, return COMMITTED and do not replace. Quiescence alone is insufficient because an effect may have occurred before b without a wrapper record; an accurate zero read alone is insufficient because execution may occur afterward. Eventual availability of both certificate and outcome observation establishes resolution liveness. A genuine known end-to-end bound after which every attempt has either committed or become permanently incapable of committing can supply quiescence, but an ordinary client timeout, queue-only expiry, or worker termination does not prove that bound.

review.rationale: With new dispatches closed, a trustworthy barrier excludes future original effects. A complete post-barrier observation determines whether a past effect exists, so zero authorizes replacement and one prohibits it. The two single-component failure cases correctly show why neither quiescence nor a zero read alone suffices.

reasoning_steps.title: Review the prior result and the strongest open obligation
reasoning_steps.argument: The supplied extract of 496ed077-19aa-4a3d-a216-0a51cf23c866 explicitly treats seal as a stronger assumed specification and warns that upstream checks do not exclude downstream work. The present derivation advances o42/o101/o105 by proving the wrapper-only obstruction under a precise nonparticipation and uncertainty model, rather than assuming seal feasible. It does not establish whether any selected service supplies a qualifying boundary or quiescence mechanism, so o38/o80 and actual-service compliance remain unresolved. Artifact 29362c57-cbcb-4127-8b3d-3976a3e3e206 is supplied only as a pointer and ledger scope description; its original proof and probability theorem were not inspected or used. The cycle-2 source itself is an incomplete extract, so omitted material remains unreviewed.

review.rationale: The visible cycle-2 steps assume seal rather than implement it and explicitly identify the upstream-check gap. Cycle 3 supplies the previously missing wrapper-level impossibility derivation while leaving actual-service compliance open. It correctly does not rely on the pointer-only cycle-1 proof.

reasoning_steps.title: Assess the evidence-linked peer handoff without transferring its theorem
reasoning_steps.argument: Handoff 87ca7ad1-e21a-4f4c-841a-5467c4cd9072 links source 9eb918fc-83c7-4ab9-a2ac-e0aec95df25a to target 29362c57-cbcb-4127-8b3d-3976a3e3e206. The supplied source extract concerns fixed finite cohorts, stable binary correctness Y at a specified horizon, reference labels Z, simultaneous audit coverage, and justified whole-cell disagreement budgets delta_c. This recovery analysis concerns an online authorization valid against future effects under an execution contract. Those assumptions and domains do not match. The target original is unavailable and the source theorem is truncated, so neither original is independently verified here. I adopt only the methodological complement: observable acceptance is not authoritative external correctness. I reject transfer of either a recovery probability bound into delta_c or an audit interval into cancellation feasibility. The handoff does not disprove either conditional approach.

review.rationale: The visible peer assumptions concern stable finite-cohort labels and justified disagreement budgets, not online authorization against every future continuation. Narrowing the transfer to the need for authoritative external evidence is justified; neither omitted theorem is needed.

reasoning_steps.title: Test the complement and specify the discriminating next check
reasoning_steps.argument: As an analytical bridge, define Y_H = 1 when exactly one actual effect has occurred by horizon H, and let Z be the wrapper's completion label. Choose H after replacement and after the delayed original in P, with no downstream notification before H. D and P can have identical wrapper observations and Z, but Y_H is respectively one and zero. Replicating either history over distinct request identities permits all completion labels to agree while the disagreement fraction is respectively zero or one. Thus these observations alone justify no nontrivial whole-cell disagreement budget; this does not challenge a certificate explicitly conditional on a valid budget. Also, Y_H = 1 before a late effect does not establish permanent cancellation safety. This narrows the next step from merely obtaining more correctness judgments to checking authoritative outcome evidence plus exclusion. The next implementation test, when a service and oracle are available, is to pause a dispatched call beyond the wrapper's last token check, obtain local cancellation, acknowledge a replacement, and then release the old call. A true exclusion mechanism must prevent the late original effect; an upstream-only mechanism permits two effects. An evaluator-only actual-effect ledger and a commit-before-barrier control are required. These are predictions and a proposed test, not measured results.

review.rationale: For the constructed histories with no distinguishing notification before H, the same wrapper label can accompany one or two effects. Repeating these admissible histories yields disagreement fractions zero or one, so those observations alone cannot justify a nontrivial budget. This is an identifiability example and proposed test, not an observed cohort or a refutation of a certificate conditional on valid budgets.

strategy_findings.skeptic_response:
The cycle-3 local result is convincing but unverified. In the discarded execution, conclusive resolution must eventually return CANCELLED because no actual commitment exists. At that finite decision prefix, a downstream execution delayed until afterward has the same wrapper records, fencing epochs, clocks, and absence replies. It therefore receives the same authorization, although the original can still commit. The legal order CANCELLED < replacement effect < original effect produces two irreversible effects. Durable local state does not exclude this continuation.

This establishes a contract-level safety–liveness obstruction, not universal recovery impossibility. Waiting or returning UNKNOWN can preserve safety but does not meet the explicitly defined conclusive-resolution requirement. The randomized scope is appropriately restricted to pointwise guarantees; no almost-sure or numerical bound is established.

The proposed escape conditions are sound as conditional specifications. Effect-boundary serialization can exclude late execution. Alternatively, certified quiescence plus a complete post-barrier outcome observation can establish both past outcome and future exclusion. Neither component alone suffices: quiescence can follow an unrecorded commitment, while an accurate zero read can precede a late effect. Eventual evidence delivery is an additional liveness premise, and replacement acknowledgment is needed for confirmed task completion.

The peer handoff is useful only as a narrowed methodological complement. Fixed-horizon correctness auditing and permanent execution exclusion have different domains. The paired histories also demonstrate why wrapper-label agreement alone cannot validate an oracle-disagreement budget. No peer interval, probability theorem, or omitted derivation is transferred.

The analytical boundary question is answered. The broader project remains partial: no service implementation, audited effect oracle, controlled intervention result, or inspected domain literature is supplied. The next feasible analytical extension should address repeated ambiguous replacements and finite deduplication retention rather than repeat this completed argument. Actual-service validation remains blocked until a selected service contract and authoritative outcome records are supplied.
